summary: Updates the IAB Charter (RFC 2850) to be consistent with version 3 of the RFC Editor Model described in RFC 9280. It is a Best Current Practice document.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice updates the IAB Charter to align it with the version 3 RFC Editor Model. It removes one phrase and replaces one sentence in RFC 2850.

questions: how did the rfc editor model change the iab charter
what does rfc 9283 change in the iab charter
what is the rfc editor model version 3
why was the iab charter updated
subtitle: Updates the IAB Charter to match version 3 of the RFC Editor Model.

tldr.problem: The IAB Charter still described responsibilities that no longer matched the RFC Editor Model version 3.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC removes the RFC Editor from a liaison-member phrase and replaces the charter's sentence about IAB approval of the RFC Editor with a reference to RFC 9280.
tldr.outcome: The IAB Charter is updated to describe the RFC Editor function under the authority of the IAB as defined by RFC 9280.

today: RFC 9283 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 2850. The unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes RFC 9283.

sections.title: Why the IAB Charter Changed
sections.content:
Version 3 of the RFC Editor Model, defined by RFC 9280, governs the RFC Series through its own mechanisms. The IAB Charter in RFC 2850 needed changes to match that model.

The charter also said the RFC Editor appoints a liaison member to the IAB, which RFC 9283 says is no longer necessary.
sections.plainLanguage: The way the RFC Series is governed changed. The IAB Charter needed edits so its wording matched the new model.

sections.title: Edits to the IAB Charter
sections.content:
In Section 1.2 of RFC 2850, the phrase the RFC Editor, is deleted from the list of ex-officio and liaison members.

In Section 2, under "The Role of the IAB" and "RFC Series and IANA", a sentence requiring IAB approval of an organization acting as RFC Editor and its general policy is replaced with: "The RFC Editor function is defined under the authority of the IAB by [RFC9280]."
sections.plainLanguage: The charter removes the RFC Editor from one membership phrase. It replaces an approval rule with a reference to the RFC Editor Model.

sections.title: Approval, IANA and Security
sections.content:
RFC 9283 is published as an IETF Best Current Practice. It was approved by the IAB and acknowledged by the Board of Trustees of the Internet Society.

The RFC has no IANA actions and says it should not affect Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC is a Best Current Practice approved by the IAB. It changes no IANA registry and is expected not to affect Internet security.

references.text: Internet Architecture Board and B. Carpenter, Ed., "Charter of the Internet Architecture Board (IAB)", BCP 39, RFC 2850, May 2000.
